description: "Translating raw Mars elevation and climate datasets into practical surface navigation tools."
summary: Existing Mars mapping platforms provide global overviews, yet astronauts conducting Extra-Vehicular Activities (EVAs) require hyperlocal, multi-layered navigation to traverse hazardous terrain safely in bulky spacesuits. [App Name] is an interactive Martian surface navigation and EVA mission-planning tool designed for human explorers at Jezero Crater. By integrating three core NASA datasets—high-resolution HiRISE/MOLA topography for slope hazard detection, THEMIS thermal inertia to distinguish solid bedrock from loose sand traps, and CRISM spectral mineralogy to pinpoint high-value science targets—our application calculates optimal walking routes that balance scientific discovery with crew safety. Additionally, a dynamic life-support estimator monitors spacesuit oxygen, battery consumption, and radiation exposure across elevation changes, empowering astronauts to plan, adapt, and execute safe Mars walks in real time.
details: Lagrange Points is a hyperlocal Martian surface navigation and survival guide built to help astronauts safely plan and execute Extra-Vehicular Activities (EVAs) on Mars. While existing planetary maps provide broad global views, explorers on foot need localized, multi-layered environmental intelligence to avoid steep crater slopes, loose dust traps, and radiation hazards while reaching high-priority scientific targets. Our interactive web interface brings these mission-critical insights into a single, easy-to-read dashboard.
